Arabic-language and national cultural unity receive official priority, while constitutional religious and cultural protections acknowledge some diversity. Recognition of minorities and refugee hosting do not show equal support for every migrant practice. Some recognised religious or refugee accommodation coexists with strong common-language and administrative expectations. Accommodation must involve public services and willingness to incur additional cost. The response reflects the identified competing institutional elements, rather than neutrality substituted for uncertainty. The sources do not document an official answer to this exact statement; the normative comparison and its stated trade-off remain uncertain.
